A stage is deployed for every push, then smoke-tested, privacy-read-back, and driven by the end-to-end suite, even when the pull request has already moved on or when the diff cannot change a deployed byte.

## Measured baseline

`node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7`, over 7 days to 2026-11-17:

| Workflow | Runs | Runner minutes | Per job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI | 153 | 312 | check 1.6m, privacy 0.4m |
| Preview | 118 | 363 | deploy 1.2m, e2e 1.9m, preview-privacy 1.7m, destroy 0.7m |
| Deploy | 60 | 243 | staging deploy 0.8m, staging-e2e 1.0m, staging-privacy 1.9m, production 0.9m |
| **All** | | **918 (131 per day, about $31 per 30 days at $0.008/minute)** | |

A pull request's required answer arrives in about 90 s. The preview stage adds about 4.8 runner-minutes and about five minutes of wall time per revision. These are GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners, so the money at stake is small; feedback time and not starting work nobody needs are the point.

## What the article's numbers do not transfer

The OpenClaw post reports 86.5% fewer runner-hours on sponsored runners over a 4M-line test suite. Here the whole suite is 82 test files and finishes in 18 s locally (62 s on a runner). Sharding, dependency-based test selection and a test-line budget would each cost more than they save at this size. What transfers is the ordering: decide before you pay for setup, and make the decision inspectable and tested.

Backtested against this repository's own history, before choosing: the superseded-revision guard would have skipped 2 of the last 100 preview runs (1.3 runner-minutes) — it pays when three or more pushes land inside one run's ~4.5 minutes, which is an agent loop rather than today's cadence. The prose-only gate covers 2 of those 100 runs (8.9 runner-minutes, ~4% of preview compute) and 7 of the last 100 pull requests, because documentation work is a real share of this repo's changes.

## Steps

- [ ] **1. Measure before changing anything.** `scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs` reads the Actions API and prints runner minutes per workflow and per job, with an estimated cost at a configurable price. Re-run it after each step.
- [ ] **2. Move the preview path rules out of YAML.** `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies a changed-path list, with `select.test.ts` beside it. The two rules that already exist (the Submission-path canary, the answer-entry Lighthouse gate) move verbatim and are locked by tests; verified against 40 real commits with no behaviour change. `preview.yml` then reads the classification once per run instead of running two inline `grep`s in three jobs.
- [ ] **3. Stop a superseded revision before it pays for a stage.** One `gh api pulls/<n>` read as the first step of the `deploy` job, before checkout or install. A revision that is no longer the head stops in about ten seconds and leaves the stage to the newer run. A failed API read deploys: being unsure is a reason to run the check.
- [ ] **4. Skip the stage when the diff cannot reach it.** Prose (`docs/`, any `*.md`), agent instructions, hooks and `scripts/` get no stage; a mixed or empty diff always deploys. `preview-privacy` and `e2e` skip with it, and the Lighthouse build no longer runs when its gate is not required.
- [ ] **5. Record the decision.** ADR 0025 (the gates, the rejected options and the backtest) and the preview section of `docs/infra.md`.
- [ ] **6. Re-measure and record the result here.** `node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7` after a week of the new workflow, posted as a comment on this issue, with feedback time read beside compute cost.

## Done when

- A prose-only pull request reaches its answer without deploying a stage, and the privacy job, the canary sweep and the Lighthouse gate still run wherever they are required.
- A push that supersedes a queued revision leaves that revision with a ten-second `deploy` job instead of a full stage.
- `ci.yml` is unchanged: typecheck, the ledgers, formatting, lint, the web build, the unit suite with coverage and the separate privacy job run on every pull request and every push to `main`.
- `deploy.yml` is unchanged: staging and production deploy after every successful `main` run, and the staging canary sweep still runs every time.
- `pnpm test scripts/ci/select.test.ts` fails if a path rule changes without being meant.
- The re-measurement in step 6 is posted here.

## Not in this issue

- **Gating the Deploy workflow by changed paths.** A `workflow_run` payload does not say how many commits a push carried, so the tip's diff can miss a Submission-path change earlier in the same push, and a privacy invariant is a release blocker (SPEC §7). Revisit only with a reliable push range, for example by diffing against the last deployed SHA.
- **`cancel-in-progress: true` on the preview group.** It interrupts a half-applied Alchemy deploy or destroy; the revision guard removes the same waste without interrupting anything.
- **Workflow-level `paths:` filters.** A filtered run reports no check at all, so a reviewer cannot tell "not needed" from "not reported".
- **Caching Playwright browsers in the `e2e` job.** Worth about 30 s per run; measure it before adding a cache key.
- **Splitting the `check` job.** The suite is the dominant step (62 s) and runs in parallel with nothing today; splitting would buy ~25 s of wall time and pay a second setup.

## Status

Steps 1–5 are drafted in a working tree and still need review, commit and one pull request. The pull request itself exercises the new path: it touches `scripts/ci` and `preview.yml`, so it gets a stage, an end-to-end run and a privacy read-back, and skips the canary sweep and the Lighthouse gate.

  "body": "The preview workflow is the largest single cost in CI, and the run decides most of its work only after it has already started. A stage is deployed for every push, then smoke-tested, privacy-read-back, and driven by the end-to-end suite, even when the pull request has already moved on or when the diff cannot change a deployed byte.

## Measured baseline

`node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7`, over 7 days to 2026-11-17:

| Workflow | Runs | Runner minutes | Per job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI | 153 | 312 | check 1.6m, privacy 0.4m |
| Preview | 118 | 363 | deploy 1.2m, e2e 1.9m, preview-privacy 1.7m, destroy 0.7m |
| Deploy | 60 | 243 | staging deploy 0.8m, staging-e2e 1.0m, staging-privacy 1.9m, production 0.9m |
| **All** | | **918 (131 per day, about $31 per 30 days at $0.008/minute)** | |

A pull request's required answer arrives in about 90 s. The preview stage adds about 4.8 runner-minutes and about five minutes of wall time per revision. These are GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners, so the money at stake is small; feedback time and not starting work nobody needs are the point.

## What the article's numbers do not transfer

The OpenClaw post reports 86.5% fewer runner-hours on sponsored runners over a 4M-line test suite. Here the whole suite is 82 test files and finishes in 18 s locally (62 s on a runner). Sharding, dependency-based test selection and a test-line budget would each cost more than they save at this size. What transfers is the ordering: decide before you pay for setup, and make the decision inspectable and tested.

Backtested against this repository's own history, before choosing: the superseded-revision guard would have skipped 2 of the last 100 preview runs (1.3 runner-minutes) — it pays when three or more pushes land inside one run's ~4.5 minutes, which is an agent loop rather than today's cadence. The prose-only gate covers 2 of those 100 runs (8.9 runner-minutes, ~4% of preview compute) and 7 of t
he last 100 pull requests, because documentation work is a real share of this repo's changes.

## Steps

- [ ] **1. Measure before changing anything.** `scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs` reads the Actions API and prints runner minutes per workflow and per job, with an estimated cost at a configurable price. Re-run it after each step.
- [ ] **2. Move the preview path rules out of YAML.** `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies a changed-path list, with `select.test.ts` beside it. The two rules that already exist (the Submission-path canary, the answer-entry Lighthouse gate) move verbatim and are locked by tests; verified against 40 real commits with no behaviour change. `preview.yml` then reads the classification once per run instead of running two inline `grep`s in three jobs.
- [ ] **3. Stop a superseded revision before it pays for a stage.** One `gh api pulls/<n>` read as the first step of the `deploy` job, before checkout or install. A revision that is no longer the head stops in about ten seconds and leaves the stage to the newer run. A failed API read deploys: being unsure is a reason to run the check.
- [ ] **4. Skip the stage when the diff cannot reach it.** Prose (`docs/`, any `*.md`), agent instructions, hooks and `scripts/` get no stage; a mixed or empty diff always deploys. `preview-privacy` and `e2e` skip with it, and the Lighthouse build no longer runs when its gate is not required.
- [ ] **5. Record the decision.** ADR 0025 (the gates, the rejected options and the backtest) and the preview section of `docs/infra.md`.
- [ ] **6. Re-measure and record the result here.** `node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7` after a week of the new workflow, posted as a comment on this issue, with feedback time read beside compute cost.

## Done when

- A prose-only pull request reaches its answer without deploying a stage, and the privacy job, the canary sweep and the Lighthouse gate still run wherever they are required.
- A push that supersedes a queued re
vision leaves that revision with a ten-second `deploy` job instead of a full stage.
- `ci.yml` is unchanged: typecheck, the ledgers, formatting, lint, the web build, the unit suite with coverage and the separate privacy job run on every pull request and every push to `main`.
- `deploy.yml` is unchanged: staging and production deploy after every successful `main` run, and the staging canary sweep still runs every time.
- `pnpm test scripts/ci/select.test.ts` fails if a path rule changes without being meant.
- The re-measurement in step 6 is posted here.

## Not in this issue

- **Gating the Deploy workflow by changed paths.** A `workflow_run` payload does not say how many commits a push carried, so the tip's diff can miss a Submission-path change earlier in the same push, and a privacy invariant is a release blocker (SPEC §7). Revisit only with a reliable push range, for example by diffing against the last deployed SHA.
- **`cancel-in-progress: true` on the preview group.** It interrupts a half-applied Alchemy deploy or destroy; the revision guard removes the same waste without interrupting anything.
- **Workflow-level `paths:` filters.** A filtered run reports no check at all, so a reviewer cannot tell "not needed" from "not reported".
- **Caching Playwright browsers in the `e2e` job.** Worth about 30 s per run; measure it before adding a cache key.
- **Splitting the `check` job.** The suite is the dominant step (62 s) and runs in parallel with nothing today; splitting would buy ~25 s of wall time and pay a second setup.

## Status

Steps 1–5 are drafted in a working tree and still need review, commit and one pull request. The pull request itself exercises the new path: it touches `scripts/ci` and `preview.yml`, so it gets a stage, an end-to-end run and a privacy read-back, and skips the canary sweep and the Lighthouse gate.

1→### Feature

**You own the design. Plan, review, verify.** Delegate implementation. Stay in the lead.

1. Trace the affected subsystem.
2. `architect` for the shape.
3. Write the throughput checkpoint as four todo items. A dimension that genuinely does not apply (single file, no fan-out) keeps its item with `n/a: <reason>` rather than being dropped:
   - **Blocking first steps.** Gates run before fan-out.
   - **Independent workstreams.** Disjoint files, services, or layers parallelize. Shared writes serialize.
10→   - **Shared mutable state.** Default to splitting the target (the **separate-before-serializing-shared-state** principle skill). Serialize only for real invariants.
   - **Smallest safe decomposition.** If one worker is best, name why.
4. Delegate code-writing to a subagent using your configured feature model (default in poteto-mode's Models section) with a specific scope (file paths, named data shape and its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**, a state machine over scattered booleans, a table/registry over branching, a typed model over repeated shape assumptions, chosen before the delegate writes logic, and success criteria). Pick each subagent's reasoning level for the job, per the Subagents section. When the implementation admits multiple valid shapes (error handling, abstraction layer, test structure), delegate via the **arena** skill instead so the runners surface the alternatives and the cross-judge guards the pick. Mandatory: no skip-with-reason escape, and Laziness Protocol does not override it (the gain is review separation, not lines saved). A subagent forbidden to spawn satisfies this by owning the diff directly with the same review separation. No "standing by" reply that waits on a nested agent. **Give every file-writing delegate its own worktree** (spawn it with `isolation: "worktree"`, or hand it an exclusive branch), and do not write files or run a suite in a worktree a delegate still holds. On Claude Code, `isolation: "worktree"` branches from the remote default branch unless the `worktree.baseRef` setting is `"head"`. When the delegate builds on commits the default branch lacks, commit them, create its worktree with `git worktree add <path> -b <delegate-branch> HEAD`, and name that base commit in the brief. Fencing a file in the brief's prose is not a lock (**principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state**). Surgical edits, re-ground against the source for upstream-derived files. Port shared-primitive improvements to all consumers and verify each. Commit liberally.
5. Verify on the matching surface. "Inconclusive" or wrong-surface is not a pass. Flag it.
6. Rebase into small, ordered commits. Stack follow-ups.
   Use the **sequence-verifiable-units** principle skill, building, verifying, and committing each small unit before the next.
7. If the design is contested, `interrogate` before shipping.
8. Run **Opening a PR**.

Code-coupled work (one feature, one migration) goes to a single owner with the checkpoint inline. That owner fans out internally after the blocking phase. Parent-level fan-out is for slices that produce independent artifacts (audits, cross-subsystem investigations, competing experiments). Rewrite the checkpoint at phase boundaries. Spawn a fresh owner rather than chaining interrupts.
20→
**Reply:** what you built, what you chose and why, the throughput checkpoint, open decisions. Tables for design alternatives.

1→---
name: architect
description: "Sketch types, signatures, and module structure before code, then stay in the loop while implementation fills in. Use for /architect, 'architect this', 'design this', or non-trivial work where jumping to code would lock in the wrong shape."
---

# Architect

On Codex, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/codex-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

10→On GitHub Copilot, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/copilot-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

On Antigravity, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/agy-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.

Before writing code, trace every system the change touches, then sketch two different shapes for it (types, signatures, module boundaries) and pick the one where each piece of state has one owner, each task has one way to do it, and callers need to know least. Redesign instead of patching if workarounds repeat.

For a large or contested design, run the **arena** skill instead of sketching alone.

20→Before closing each implementation unit or handing its contract to the next worker, compare accepted deviations with the saved sketch and rationale. Once the owner or review process accepts a change, update the affected parts of the sketch and record who accepted it. Keep unaccepted changes and unresolved disagreements visible, and never edit the sketch merely to justify what was implemented.

1→name: Preview

# One stage per pull request: `pr-<number>`, on pr-<number>.dashboard.surveybeat.app and
# pr-<number>.submit.surveybeat.app. Destroyed when the pull request closes.
# Alchemy state lives in the Cloudflare state store (see docs/infra.md for the one-time bootstrap).

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]
10→
permissions:
  contents: read
  deployments: write
  pull-requests: read

# One run per pull request at a time, and never cancel a running deploy or destroy.
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
20→
env:
  STAGE: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}

jobs:
  # Decides what this revision needs before any stage work starts (docs/adr/0026-preview-stage-gates.md).
  # The path rules live in scripts/ci/select.mjs and are locked by scripts/ci/select.test.ts.
  select:
30→    # Fork and Dependabot pull requests get no secrets, so they get no stage (CI's check and privacy still run).
    if: >-
      github.event.action != 'closed'
      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
      && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      head: ${{ steps.head.outputs.head }}
      stage: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.stage }}
40→      canary: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.canary }}
      lighthouse: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.lighthouse }}
    steps:
      # Runs before any checkout. A failed read keeps the stage: being unsure is a reason to run.
      - name: Stop a superseded revision
        id: head
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
50→          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          if current=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR" --jq .head.sha) && [ "$current" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Revision $HEAD_SHA is no longer the head of #$PR ($current): a newer revision owns the stage."
            echo "head=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "head=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Check out the classifier
        if: steps.head.outputs.head == 'true'
60→        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: scripts/ci
      - name: Classify the changed paths
        id: classify
        if: steps.head.outputs.head == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
70→          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        # The compare endpoint is addressed by commit, so the list cannot be stale after a push. It matches the
        # old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename. It caps at 3000 files, so a list that
        # long may be cut short and keeps every gate.
        run: |
          if gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" \
              --jq '.files[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt" \
            && [ "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt")" -lt 3000 ]; then
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt"
          else
80→            echo "The changed files could not be read in full: every stage gate is required."
            printf 'stage=true\ncanary=true\nlighthouse=true\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  deploy:
    needs: select
    if: needs.select.outputs.head == 'true' && needs.select.outputs.stage == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment:
90→      name: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      url: https://${{ env.STAGE }}.dashboard.surveybeat.app
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

name: Preview

# One stage per pull request: `pr-<number>`, on pr-<number>.dashboard.surveybeat.app and
# pr-<number>.submit.surveybeat.app. Destroyed when the pull request closes.
# Alchemy state lives in the Cloudflare state store (see docs/infra.md for the one-time bootstrap).

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  deployments: write
  pull-requests: read

# One run per pull request at a time, and never cancel a running deploy or destroy.
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  STAGE: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
  CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}

jobs:
  # Decides what this revision needs before any stage work starts (docs/adr/0026-preview-stage-gates.md).
  # The path rules live in scripts/ci/select.mjs and are locked by scripts/ci/select.test.ts.
  select:
    # Fork and Dependabot pull requests get no secrets, so they get no stage (CI's check and privacy still run).
    if: >-
      github.event.action != 'closed'
      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
      && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      head: ${{ steps.head.outputs.head }}
      stage: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.stage }}
      canary: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.canary }}
      lighthouse: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.lighthouse }}
    steps:
      # Runs before any checkout. A failed read keeps the stage: being unsure is a reason to run.
      - name: Stop a superseded revision
        id: head
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          if current=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR" --jq .head.sha) && [ "$current" != "$HEAD_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Revision $HEAD_SHA is no longer the head of #$PR ($current): a newer revision owns the stage."
            echo "head=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "head=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Check out the classifier
        if: steps.head.outputs.head == 'true'
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          sparse-checkout: scripts/ci
      - name: Classify the changed paths
        id: classify
        if: steps.head.outputs.head == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        # The compare endpoint is addressed by commit, so the list cannot be stale after a push. It matches the
        # old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename. It caps at 3000 files, so a list that
        # long may be cut short and keeps every gate.
        run: |
          if gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" \
              --jq '.files[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt" \
            && [ "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt")" -lt 3000 ]; then
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt"
          else
            echo "The changed files could not be read in full: every stage gate is required."
            printf 'stage=true\ncanary=true\nlighthouse=true\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  deploy:
    needs: select
    if: needs.select.outputs.head == 'true' && needs.select.outputs.stage == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment:
      name: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      url: https://${{ env.STAGE }}.dashboard.surveybeat.app
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Build the web app
        run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
      # The Organization-creation allowlist comes from infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml; only the AI key is a secret.
      - name: Deploy the stage
        run: pnpm exec alchemy deploy infra/alchemy.run.ts --stage "$STAGE" --yes --no-input
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      - name: Smoke test
        run: node infra/scripts/smoke.ts "https://$STAGE.dashboard.surveybeat.app" "https://$STAGE.submit.surveybeat.app"

  # Preview-stage privacy checks (privacy suite design, issue #25): A7 on the deployed stage.
  # The read-back runs on every stage. The canary sweep is required only when select.mjs finds a PR touching
  # what the Submission path is built from; otherwise the step passes without running.
  preview-privacy:
    needs: [select, deploy]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Read back the Submission Worker's deployed settings
        run: pnpm check:observability --stage "$STAGE"
      - name: Canary sweep with a positive control
        if: needs.select.outputs.canary == 'true'
        run: pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage "$STAGE" "https://$STAGE.dashboard.surveybeat.app" "https://$STAGE.submit.surveybeat.app"

  # End-to-end tests: the suite on the PR stage, then the SPEC §7 flow on the runner's local stage.
  # The Lighthouse gate runs only when select.mjs finds an answer entry change, and it reads the built app.
  e2e:
    needs: [select, deploy]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      # The stage tests run against the deployed stage, and the flow's Playwright web server builds the app itself.
      - name: Build the web app
        if: needs.select.outputs.lighthouse == 'true'
        run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
      - name: Install Chromium
        run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Lighthouse CI gate (performance budgets)
        if: needs.select.outputs.lighthouse == 'true'
        run: pnpm test:lighthouse
      - name: Lighthouse gate positive control (a planted render-blocking stylesheet must be caught)
        if: needs.select.outputs.lighthouse == 'true'
        run: pnpm test:lighthouse
        env:
          LIGHTHOUSE_PLANT_RENDER_BLOCKING: "1"
      - name: End-to-end tests
        run: pnpm test:e2e
        env:
          E2E_BASE_URL: https://${{ env.STAGE }}.dashboard.surveybeat.app
      # The flow needs the test routes and captured email, which only a test_ stage has, so it runs on the runner's local stage.
      - name: SPEC §7 flow on the local stage
        run: pnpm test:e2e flow.spec.ts --project chromium
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: e2e-traces
          path: test-results/e2e
          retention-days: 7
      - if: always() && needs.select.outputs.lighthouse == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: lighthouse-reports
          path: test-results/lighthouse
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

  destroy:
    if: >-
      github.event.action == 'closed'
      && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
      && github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      # The head commit, because the merge ref is gone once the pull request is merged.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@73e46992e05b19abd31f2f3c20e0e7370d762115 # v6.1.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .node-version
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
      - name: Destroy the stage
        run: pnpm exec alchemy destroy infra/alchemy.run.ts --stage "$STAGE" --yes --no-input
        env:
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}

1→# Preview stages are gated by what the revision changes

The preview workflow was the largest single CI cost, and it decided most of its work only after it had started. Every push deployed a stage, smoke tested it, read back its privacy settings and ran the end-to-end suite. That happened even when the pull request had already moved on, and even when the diff could not change a deployed byte.

## Context

Baseline from `node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7`, over the seven days to 2026-11-17:

| Workflow | Runs | Runner minutes | Per job |
10→| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI | 153 | 312 | check 1.6m, privacy 0.4m |
| Preview | 118 | 363 | deploy 1.2m, e2e 1.9m, preview-privacy 1.7m, destroy 0.7m |
| Deploy | 60 | 243 | staging deploy 0.8m, staging-e2e 1.0m, staging-privacy 1.9m, production 0.9m |
| All | | 918 (131 per day, about $31 per 30 days at $0.008 a minute) | |

A pull request's required answer arrives in about 90 seconds. The preview stage adds about 4.8 runner minutes and about five minutes of wall time per revision. The runners are GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, so the money at stake is small. Feedback time and work nobody needs are the point.

The whole test suite is 82 test files and finishes in 18 seconds locally. At this size, sharding and dependency-based test selection would cost more than they save. What transfers is the order: decide before paying for setup, and make the decision inspectable and tested.

20→Backtest against this repository's last 100 preview runs:

- The superseded-revision guard would have skipped 2 of them (1.3 runner minutes). It pays when three or more pushes land inside one run's ~4.5 minutes, which is an agent loop rather than today's cadence.
- The prose-only gate covers 2 of them (8.9 runner minutes, about 4% of preview compute) and 7 of the last 100 pull requests. Documentation work is a real share of this repository's changes.

## Decision

The preview workflow starts with a `select` job. It runs before checkout and before any install, and it sets four outputs: `head`, `stage`, `canary` and `lighthouse`.

- **Superseded guard.** The first step reads the pull request's current head SHA. If the revision is no longer the head, `head` is false and every later job in the run is skipped. A newer revision owns the stage. If the read fails, `head` is true: being unsure is a reason to run.
30→- **Path rules in tested code.** `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies the changed files, and `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` locks every rule. The canary rule (the Submission path) and the Lighthouse rule (the answer entry) are the regular expressions the workflow already used, moved verbatim. The canary also covers `scripts/ci/`, because a pull request that changes the gates must run them.
- **Changed files.** The list comes from the compare endpoint, addressed by the base and head SHAs of the pull request. It matches the old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename, so a rename away from a gated path stays gated. The endpoint caps at 3000 files, and a list that long keeps every gate.
- **Prose-only gate.** `stage` is false only when the list is non-empty and every file is prose or tooling that cannot reach a deployed stage: under `docs/`, any `*.md` file, the agent instruction directories, `.githooks/`, `skills-lock.json`, or the root `scripts/` (not `infra/scripts/` and not `scripts/ci/`). An empty list, a mixed list or any other path deploys. A canary or Lighthouse path always keeps the stage, even when it is markdown.
- **Jobs.** `deploy` runs when `head` and `stage` are on. `preview-privacy` and `e2e` need `deploy`, so they skip with it. The canary sweep runs only when `canary` is on. The Lighthouse gate and its app build run only when `lighthouse` is on.
- **Failure modes.** A failed read of the pull request keeps the stage. A failed read of the changed files turns on all three gates.

`ci.yml` and `deploy.yml` do not change. Every pull request still runs the check job and the privacy job, and every merge to `main` still deploys staging and production.

## Considered options

40→- **Gating the Deploy workflow by changed paths.** Rejected. A `workflow_run` payload does not say how many commits a push carried, so the tip's diff can miss a Submission-path change earlier in the same push. A privacy invariant is a release blocker (SPEC §7). Revisit only with a reliable push range, for example by diffing against the last deployed SHA.
- **`cancel-in-progress: true` on the preview group.** Rejected. It interrupts a half-applied Alchemy deploy or destroy. The revision guard removes the same waste without interrupting anything.
- **Workflow-level `paths:` filters.** Rejected. A filtered run reports no check at all, so a reviewer cannot tell "not needed" from "not reported".
- **Caching Playwright browsers in the `e2e` job.** Rejected for now. It is worth about 30 seconds per run. Measure it before adding a cache key.
- **Splitting the `check` job.** Rejected. The suite is the dominant step (62 seconds on a runner) and runs in parallel with nothing today. Splitting would buy about 25 seconds of wall time and pay for a second setup.

## Consequences

- The path rules are code. A change to a rule fails `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` until the test is updated on purpose.
- The rules come from the revision under test, the same as the workflow file itself. A pull request that edits `scripts/ci/select.mjs` is classified by its own copy.
50→- A change to `scripts/ci/` always deploys and runs the canary sweep, because it changes the gates. Other root `scripts/` paths stay prose and do not deploy.
- The gate classifies the whole PR diff against its base, not the one push. So a stage deployed by an earlier revision stays until the PR closes, even if the diff later becomes prose-only. A prose-only revision does not tear it down.
- The effect on feedback time and compute is to be measured after a week of the new workflow, as the issue's step 6 says.

# Preview stages are gated by what the revision changes

The preview workflow was the largest single CI cost, and it decided most of its work only after it had started. Every push deployed a stage, smoke tested it, read back its privacy settings and ran the end-to-end suite. That happened even when the pull request had already moved on, and even when the diff could not change a deployed byte.

## Context

Baseline from `node scripts/ci/runner-minutes.mjs --days 7`, over the seven days to 2026-11-17:

| Workflow | Runs | Runner minutes | Per job |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI | 153 | 312 | check 1.6m, privacy 0.4m |
| Preview | 118 | 363 | deploy 1.2m, e2e 1.9m, preview-privacy 1.7m, destroy 0.7m |
| Deploy | 60 | 243 | staging deploy 0.8m, staging-e2e 1.0m, staging-privacy 1.9m, production 0.9m |
| All | | 918 (131 per day, about $31 per 30 days at $0.008 a minute) | |

A pull request's required answer arrives in about 90 seconds. The preview stage adds about 4.8 runner minutes and about five minutes of wall time per revision. The runners are GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`, so the money at stake is small. Feedback time and work nobody needs are the point.

The whole test suite is 82 test files and finishes in 18 seconds locally. At this size, sharding and dependency-based test selection would cost more than they save. What transfers is the order: decide before paying for setup, and make the decision inspectable and tested.

Backtest against this repository's last 100 preview runs:

- The superseded-revision guard would have skipped 2 of them (1.3 runner minutes). It pays when three or more pushes land inside one run's ~4.5 minutes, which is an agent loop rather than today's cadence.
- The prose-only gate covers 2 of them (8.9 runner minutes, about 4% of preview compute) and 7 of the last 100 pull requests. Documentation work is a real share of this repository's changes.

## Decision

The preview workflow starts with a `select` job. It runs before checkout and before any install, and it sets four outputs: `head`, `stage`, `canary` and `lighthouse`.

- **Superseded guard.** The first step reads the pull request's current head SHA. If the revision is no longer the head, `head` is false and every later job in the run is skipped. A newer revision owns the stage. If the read fails, `head` is true: being unsure is a reason to run.
- **Path rules in tested code.** `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies the changed files, and `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` locks every rule. The canary rule (the Submission path) and the Lighthouse rule (the answer entry) are the regular expressions the workflow already used, moved verbatim. The canary also covers `scripts/ci/`, because a pull request that changes the gates must run them.
- **Changed files.** The list comes from the compare endpoint, addressed by the base and head SHAs of the pull request. It matches the old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename, so a rename away from a gated path stays gated. The endpoint caps at 3000 files, and a list that long keeps every gate.
- **Prose-only gate.** `stage` is false only when the list is non-empty and every file is prose or tooling that cannot reach a deployed stage: under `docs/`, any `*.md` file, the agent instruction directories, `.githooks/`, `skills-lock.json`, or the root `scripts/` (not `infra/scripts/` and not `scripts/ci/`). An empty list, a mixed list or any other path deploys. A canary or Lighthouse path always keeps the stage, even when it is markdown.
- **Jobs.** `deploy` runs when `head` and `stage` are on. `preview-privacy` and `e2e` need `deploy`, so they skip with it. The canary sweep runs only when `canary` is on. The Lighthouse gate and its app build run only when `lighthouse` is on.
- **Failure modes.** A failed read of the pull request keeps the stage. A failed read of the changed files turns on all three gates.

`ci.yml` and `deploy.yml` do not change. Every pull request still runs the check job and the privacy job, and every merge to `main` still deploys staging and production.

## Considered options

- **Gating the Deploy workflow by changed paths.** Rejected. A `workflow_run` payload does not say how many commits a push carried, so the tip's diff can miss a Submission-path change earlier in the same push. A privacy invariant is a release blocker (SPEC §7). Revisit only with a reliable push range, for example by diffing against the last deployed SHA.
- **`cancel-in-progress: true` on the preview group.** Rejected. It interrupts a half-applied Alchemy deploy or destroy. The revision guard removes the same waste without interrupting anything.
- **Workflow-level `paths:` filters.** Rejected. A filtered run reports no check at all, so a reviewer cannot tell "not needed" from "not reported".
- **Caching Playwright browsers in the `e2e` job.** Rejected for now. It is worth about 30 seconds per run. Measure it before adding a cache key.
- **Splitting the `check` job.** Rejected. The suite is the dominant step (62 seconds on a runner) and runs in parallel with nothing today. Splitting would buy about 25 seconds of wall time and pay for a second setup.

## Consequences

- The path rules are code. A change to a rule fails `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` until the test is updated on purpose.
- The rules come from the revision under test, the same as the workflow file itself. A pull request that edits `scripts/ci/select.mjs` is classified by its own copy.
- A change to `scripts/ci/` always deploys and runs the canary sweep, because it changes the gates. Other root `scripts/` paths stay prose and do not deploy.
- The gate classifies the whole PR diff against its base, not the one push. So a stage deployed by an earlier revision stays until the PR closes, even if the diff later becomes prose-only. A prose-only revision does not tear it down.
- The effect on feedback time and compute is to be measured after a week of the new workflow, as the issue's step 6 says.

The issue was largely implemented and merged as PR #264.

The issue remains open because step 6 requires re-measuring after a week. The PR merged yesterday, so that step is not yet due. The issue body still lists steps 1-5 as drafted, which is stale. I could run an early measurement now, but the issue specifies waiting a week. I should also check for bugs introduced after the merge.

I will check recent workflow runs and tests to verify the implementation. I also noticed that the preview-privacy and e2e jobs lack `if:` conditions and only depend on `needs: deploy`.

GitHub Actions skips dependent jobs when a needed job is skipped. The preview-privacy and e2e jobs lack `if:` conditions, so they would be skipped if deploy is skipped.

I verified that skipped select jobs also correctly skip deploy and dependent jobs. I am now looking for a potential bug in the superseded check: the logic treats an uncertain API read as a reason to run the check.

The superseded check logic is sound. API failures and SHA mismatches both correctly set head to false. GitHub Actions handles errors safely. The classify step only runs when head is true.

I spotted a potential bug in the classify step. If the classifier crashes, the job fails and deploy is skipped entirely. The issue says "being unsure is a reason to run the check," so a classifier failure should probably still allow deployment rather than blocking it.

A classifier crash would fail the select job. That would skip preview-privacy, which is a required check. A skipped required check could block the pull request. The ADR only covers failed file reads, not script crashes.

AGENTS.md states that a skipped workflow check counts as passed. If the select job crashes, preview-privacy and e2e are skipped but still count as passed. This means a broken classifier could let a pull request pass while deploy, preview-privacy, and e2e are all skipped.

A classifier crash would let a pull request merge without running e2e or preview-privacy. The issue only mandates turning on all gates for a failed file read, not for script crashes. A script crash is a bug in the PR itself, so the workflow should fail. The required checks are named jobs, not the workflow as a whole.

I will check branch protection settings and recent preview runs to see if the classifier crash hole is actually a problem in practice. The merge was only one day ago, so step six is not yet due. I need to verify whether any CI bugs surfaced after the merge, since the user wants the issue properly finished.

CodeRabbit found a real bug that was merged anyway.

The bug is a 300-file cap on the GitHub compare endpoint. When documentation-only files hit that limit, preview deployment and privacy checks are skipped because the intended fail-open fallback never triggers.

The script paginates the compare endpoint but only checks the first page's line count. It never verifies whether the full list was retrieved, so the fail-open fallback never triggers.

The GitHub compare endpoint itself caps the files array at 300 total. It does not paginate the way the script assumes. The `wc -l < 3000` check therefore never catches a truncated response, so the fail-open fallback never triggers.

The comment and ADR both incorrectly claim the endpoint caps at 3000 files. The GitHub API actually limits it to 300. If the first 300 files are all prose, the script sets stage=false and skips preview deployment and privacy checks entirely. The fail-open fallback never triggers because the line count stays below 3000 even when the list is truncated.

The GitHub documentation recommends the Git trees API for retrieving more than 300 files. The compare endpoint may support `per_page` pagination in newer API versions, but the exact limits are unclear.

Runner-minutes usage is understated because step 6 measurement is inaccurate.

Issue 230 remains open despite the merged implementation. Step 6 is still pending after only one day. The issue checkboxes are not updated. The issue body still shows "drafted, needs PR".

The next step is unclear.

The most valuable remaining work is fixing the 300-file truncation hole so large PRs cannot silently skip the stage. Runner-minutes accuracy issues before step 6 measurement may also need fixing.

I will retrieve the actual CodeRabbit review comments rather than the summary. I also need to verify the bug by reading the GitHub API documentation.

The 300-file truncation bug violates the issue's acceptance criteria. The done-when requirement explicitly states that privacy, canary, and Lighthouse gates must still run wherever they are required. A large diff whose first 300 files are prose would skip privacy read-back even if later files touch the submission path.

I will examine the detailed CodeRabbit review comments, the tests, and the runner-minutes implementation to understand the remaining findings. This is a bug fix on an existing feature, so the poteto playbook calls for an architect role followed by delegation.

The bug means steps 2 through 4 are not fully correct. The privacy read-back is skipped entirely when the stage is bypassed, not merely the canary sweep. I will read the review comments and the compare API documentation to decide the fix.

The issue intentionally skips the stage for prose-only diffs. The bug is only when the GitHub compare API truncates the file list and the script wrongly assumes it is prose-only. The fix should detect truncation by checking if the returned file count equals 300, since the API does not expose an official `truncated` flag.

The pull request files endpoint is a viable alternative to the compare endpoint. It supports pagination with 100 files per page, can retrieve up to 3000 files, and includes previous filenames for renames. This would eliminate the 300-file truncation limit entirely.

The pull request files endpoint was rejected because a newer push could race between the SHA check and the file read, making the diff stale. The compare-by-SHA endpoint avoids this race, so it should remain. The fix is to keep the compare-by-SHA approach and simply detect truncation when the returned file count reaches 300.

A community discussion suggests the GitHub compare API may support `page` and `per_page` parameters for the files array, though the exact maximum is unclear. GitHub GraphQL `compare` or `pullRequest.files` with pagination is another possible alternative. The plan is to read the CodeRabbit comments, the select tests, and the workflow cap check, confirm the API behavior, and fix the truncation detection so any incomplete list fails open.

The `--paginate` flag likely fails to retrieve the remaining files because the GitHub compare API does not return a Link header when the list is truncated. This leaves the script with only the first 300 files, which it treats as a prose-only diff because the line count stays below 3000. The proposed fix is to fail open whenever the returned file count reaches 300, since the API offers no official truncation signal. This introduces a small false-positive risk for PRs that happen to contain exactly 300 files, but it is the safer direction.

Three concrete fixes are under consideration. The first is to fail open whenever the returned file count reaches 300, accepting a small false-positive risk for a 300-file prose-only PR. The second is to paginate the compare endpoint properly using page parameters until a short page is encountered, which is more accurate but more complex. The third is to switch to the pulls files API after confirming the head SHA still matches, which paginates correctly up to 3000 files and avoids the 300-file cap entirely.

# REST API endpoints for commits

Use the REST API to interact with commits.

> [!NOTE]
> Most endpoints use `Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-TOKEN>` and `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` headers, plus `X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2026-03-10`. Curl examples below omit these standard headers for brevity.

## List commits

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits
```

Signature verification object
The response will include a verification object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the verification object:

NameTypeDescriptionverifiedbooleanIndicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified.reasonstringThe reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in table below.signaturestringThe signature that was extracted from the commit.payloadstringThe value that was signed.verified_atstringThe date the signature was verified by GitHub.
These are the possible values for reason in the verification object:

ValueDescriptionexpired_keyThe key that made the signature is expired.not_signing_keyThe "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature.gpgverify_errorThere was an error communicating with the signature verification service.gpgverify_unavailableThe signature verification service is currently unavailable.unsignedThe object does not include a signature.unknown_signature_typeA non-PGP signature was found in the commit.no_userNo user was associated with the committer email address in the commit.unverified_emailThe committer email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account.bad_emailThe committer email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature.unknown_keyThe key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account.malformed_signatureThere was an error parsing the signature.invalidThe signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature.validNone of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified.

### Parameters

#### Headers

- **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

- **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`sha`** (string)
  SHA or branch to start listing commits from. Default: the repository’s default branch (usually main).

- **`path`** (string)
  Only commits containing this file path will be returned.

- **`author`** (string)
  GitHub username or email address to use to filter by commit author.

- **`committer`** (string)
  GitHub username or email address to use to filter by commit committer.

- **`since`** (string)
  Only show results that were last updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Due to limitations of Git, timestamps must be between 1970-01-01 and 2099-12-31 (inclusive) or unexpected results may be returned.

- **`until`** (string)
  Only commits before this date will be returned. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Due to limitations of Git, timestamps must be between 1970-01-01 and 2099-12-31 (inclusive) or unexpected results may be returned.

- **`per_page`** (integer)
  The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `30`

- **`page`** (integer)
  The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `1`

### HTTP response status codes

- **200** - OK

- **400** - Bad Request

- **404** - Resource not found

- **409** - Conflict

- **422** - Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.

- **429** - The request could not be processed due to heavy server load. Please try again.

- **500** - Internal Error

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X GET \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/commits
```

**Response schema (Status: 200):**

Array of `Commit`:
  * `url`: required, string, format: uri
  * `sha`: required, string
  * `node_id`: required, string
  * `html_url`: required, string, format: uri
  * `comments_url`: required, string, format: uri
  * `commit`: required, object:
    * `url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `author`: required, any of:
      * **null**
      * **Git User**
        * `name`: string
        * `email`: string
        * `date`: string, format: date-time
    * `committer`: required, any of:
      * **null**
      * **Git User** (see above)
    * `message`: required, string
    * `comment_count`: required, integer
    * `tree`: required, object:
      * `sha`: required, string
      * `url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `verification`: `Verification`:
      * `verified`: required, boolean
      * `reason`: required, string
      * `payload`: required, string or null
      * `signature`: required, string or null
      * `verified_at`: required, string or null
  * `author`: required, one of:
    * **Simple User**
      * `name`: string or null
      * `email`: string or null
      * `login`: required, string
      * `id`: required, integer, format: int64
      * `node_id`: required, string
      * `avatar_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `gravatar_id`: required, string or null
      * `url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `html_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `followers_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `following_url`: required, string
      * `gists_url`: required, string
      * `starred_url`: required, string
      * `subscriptions_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `organizations_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `repos_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `events_url`: required, string
      * `received_events_url`: required, string, format: uri
      * `type`: required, string
      * `site_admin`: required, boolean
      * `starred_at`: string
      * `user_view_type`: string
    * **Empty Object**
  * `committer`: required, one of:
    * **Simple User** (see above)
    * **Empty Object** (see above)
  * `parents`: required, array of objects:
    * `sha`: required, string
    * `url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `html_url`: string, format: uri
  * `stats`: object:
    * `additions`: integer
    * `deletions`: integer
    * `total`: integer
  * `files`: array of `Diff Entry`:
    * `sha`: required, string or null
    * `filename`: required, string
    * `status`: required, string, enum: `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `renamed`, `copied`, `changed`, `unchanged`
    * `additions`: required, integer

    * `changes`: required, integer
    * `blob_url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `raw_url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `contents_url`: required, string, format: uri
    * `patch`: string
    * `previous_filename`: string

## List branches for HEAD commit

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{commit_sha}/branches-where-head
```

Protected branches are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations, and in public and private repositories with GitHub Pro, GitHub Team, GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and GitHub Enterprise Server. For more information, see GitHub's products in the GitHub Help documentation.
Returns all branches where the given commit SHA is the HEAD, or latest commit for the branch.

### Parameters

#### Headers

- **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

- **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`commit_sha`** (string) (required)
  The SHA of the commit.

### HTTP response status codes

- **200** - OK

- **409** - Conflict

- **422** - Validation failed, or the endpoint has been spammed.

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X GET \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/COMMIT_SHA/branches-where-head
```

**Response schema (Status: 200):**

Array of `Branch Short`:
  * `name`: required, string
  * `commit`: required, object:
    * `sha`: required, string
    * `url`: required, string
  * `protected`: required, boolean

## List pull requests associated with a commit

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{commit_sha}/pulls
```

Lists the merged pull request that introduced the commit to the repository. If the commit is not present in the default branch, it will return merged and open pull requests associated with the commit.
To list the open or merged pull requests associated with a branch, you can set the commit_sha parameter to the branch name.

### Parameters

#### Headers

- **`accept`** (string)
  Setting to `application/vnd.github+json` is recommended.

#### Path and query parameters

- **`owner`** (string) (required)
  The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`repo`** (string) (required)
  The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

- **`commit_sha`** (string) (required)
  The SHA of the commit.

- **`per_page`** (integer)
  The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `30`

- **`page`** (integer)
  The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see "Using pagination in the REST API."
  Default: `1`

### HTTP response status codes

- **200** - OK

- **409** - Conflict

### Code examples

#### Example

**Request:**

```curl
curl -L \
  -X GET \

## Get a commit

Returns the contents of a single commit reference. You must have read access for the repository to use this endpoint.
Note

If there are more than 300 files in the commit diff and the default JSON media type is requested, the response will include pagination link headers for the remaining files, up to a limit of 3000 files. Each page contains the static commit information, and the only changes are to the file listing.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "Media types." Pagination query parameters are not supported for these media types.

application/vnd.github.diff: Returns the diff of the commit. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
application/vnd.github.patch: Returns the patch of the commit. Diffs with binary data will have no patch property. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
application/vnd.github.sha: Returns the commit's SHA-1 hash. You can use this endpoint to check if a remote reference's SHA-1 hash is the same as your local reference's SHA-1 hash by providing the local SHA-1 reference as the ETag.

## Get a commit

```
GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/{ref}
```

Returns the contents of a single commit reference. You must have read access for the repository to use this endpoint.
Note

If there are more than 300 files in the commit diff and the default JSON media type is requested, the response will include pagination link headers for the remaining files, up to a limit of 3000 files. Each page contains the static commit information, and the only changes are to the file listing.

This endpoint supports the following custom media types. For more information, see "Media types." Pagination query parameters are not supported for these media types.

application/vnd.github.diff: Returns the diff of the commit. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
application/vnd.github.patch: Returns the patch of the commit. Diffs with binary data will have no patch property. Larger diffs may time out and return a 5xx status code.
application/vnd.github.sha: Returns the commit's SHA-1 hash. You can use this endpoint to check if a remote reference's SHA-1 hash is the same as your local reference's SHA-1 hash by providing the local SHA-1 reference as the ETag.

Signature verification object
The response will include a verification object that describes the result of verifying the commit's signature. The following fields are included in the verification object:

NameTypeDescriptionverifiedbooleanIndicates whether GitHub considers the signature in this commit to be verified.reasonstringThe reason for verified value. Possible values and their meanings are enumerated in table below.signaturestringThe signature that was extracted from the commit.payloadstringThe value that was signed.verified_atstringThe date the signature was verified by GitHub.
These are the possible values for reason in the verification object:

ValueDescriptionexpired_keyThe key that made the signature is expired.not_signing_keyThe "signing" flag is not among the usage flags in the GPG key that made the signature.gpgverify_errorThere was an error communicating with the signature verification service.gpgverify_unavailableThe signature verification service is currently unavailable.unsignedThe object does not include a signature.unknown_signature_typeA non-PGP signature was found in the commit.no_userNo user was associated with the committer email address in the commit.unverified_emailThe committer email address in the commit was associated with a user, but the email address is not verified on their account.bad_emailThe committer email address in the commit is not included in the identities of the PGP key that made the signature.unknown_keyThe key that made the signature has not been registered with any user's account.malformed_signatureThere was an error parsing the signature.invalidThe signature could not be cryptographically verified using the key whose key-id was found in the signature.validNone of the above errors applied, so the signature is considered to be verified.

# TypeScript best practices

On Muse, read the [platform mapping](../poteto-mode/references/muse-tools.md), including its per-skill notes, before following this skill.
10→
Apply the **type-system-discipline** principle skill first.

| Rule | Summary |
|------|---------|
| Discriminated unions | Model variants with a `kind` literal discriminant so impossible states can't be represented. No optional-field bags. |
| Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`. |
| Constructive modeling | Build the shape so the illegal value can't be constructed. `[T, ...T[]]` for non-empty, `[T, T][]` for even length, `start` plus `duration` for a range. Not a runtime guard, not a wish for refinement types. |
| Simplest total type | Keep `T[]` while every operation on it stays total. Strengthen to `NonEmpty<T>` only where the loose type forces `!`, a cast, or a "should never happen" throw. |
| `unknown` over `any` | External data is `unknown`. |
20→| Schemas before guards | Before hand-writing a property-by-property type guard, use the repository's runtime schema library and infer the type from the schema, such as `z.infer`. |
| No `as` casts | Every `as` is a runtime crash waiting. Cast only after validation. |
| Narrowing hierarchy | Discriminant switch > `in` operator > `typeof`/`instanceof` > user-defined type guard > `as`. |
| Type guards | Must verify the claim. A lying guard is worse than `as` because the bug hides behind a name that says it's safe. Name them `isX` or `hasX`. |
| Exhaustiveness | Inline `const _exhaustive: never = x;` in default arms so the compiler errors when a new variant is added. |
| `satisfies` over `as` | Validates the value without widening literal types. |
| Boundary validation | Parse where data crosses in, into a named domain type. `Record<string, unknown>` (however spelled) stops at that parse. Trust types inside. See the **boundary-discipline** principle skill. |
| Schema-derived types | Reach for `Pick`/`Omit`/`Parameters`/`ReturnType`/`Awaited`/`typeof` before declaring a new interface. |
| Object args | Pass objects, not positional, so argument order is self-documenting. Skip on hot paths (per-frame render, tokenizers, parsers). |
| Real tests | Don't mock what you can run. Prefer the framework's real test primitives with leak/disposable checks, and verify UI in a running build. Mock only what you can't run locally. |
30→| Structured telemetry | Prefer structured logger diagnostics with enough context to debug from an id. No `console.log` in shipped code. |

# Laziness Protocol

- **Consolidate decisions.** Do not repeat the same choice in several places. Put it behind one source of truth and pass the result as a simple flag.

name: principle-fix-root-causes
description: "Apply when debugging. Trace each symptom back to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there. A guard is a fix only when the state it handles is legitimate."
user-invocable: false
---

# Fix Root Causes

Fix the fault, not the place where it surfaced. The root cause is the first place the system did something it should not do, or failed to handle a state it should handle.
10→
- Reproduce first. Ask "why" until the answer is a wrong decision in the code. When stuck, instrument and read the actual state.
- Ask whether the state that triggered the symptom is legitimate. If it is, handle it where the code broke. If it should never exist, a check there hides the bug, so find what produced it. Guards, retries, swallowed errors, clamped values, and discarded state are the usual ways to hide a bug.
- Fix the pattern, not the instance. Find every place with the same fault.
- If the deciding fact took a deep dig, propose the cheap, always-on signal that would have shown it at first look.

1→---
name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
description: "Apply when you write, change, or keep a test. Assert what the code's users can observe, so that the test fails when that behavior breaks and keeps passing when only the internals change."
user-invocable: false
---

# Test Behavior, Not Implementation

A test is a claim about what users of the code can observe through its interface: return values, errors, state they can read back, and effects on outside systems. Private helpers, internal call order, and intermediate data are implementation.
10→
Judge each test against two imagined edits:

- **Break the behavior** (a wrong value, a skipped or doubled effect). If the test still passes, it proves nothing. The usual causes are a loose assertion, an expected value computed by the code under test, and an assertion on data the test built itself.
- **Change the internals** and keep every observable result. If the test fails, it is pinned to the implementation.

Keep a test that catches the first edit and survives the second. Rewrite or delete the rest. Drive the code through its public interface with a concrete input, and derive the expected value from the requirement. What an external service receives is behavior. A call to an internal helper is not. Pair "this never happens" with a case where it does happen. Assert the error type that callers branch on, not the message. A constant pin is behavior when the value is a promise to users, such as a documented default, so name that promise.

30→CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... pnpm check:observability --stage dev-yourname
CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=... CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=... pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage dev-yourname <main-url> <submission-url>
pnpm test:e2e                              # local stage: builds the app, runs `alchemy dev` on infra/tests/e2e/stack.ts
E2E_BASE_URL=<main-url> pnpm test:e2e      # the same specs against a deployed stage
                                           # once: pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium
```

Values for those commands come from `.env.schema`, which declares every variable the deploy, the e2e suite and the stage scripts read and is committed. Real values go in `.env.local`, which is not; `pnpm env:check` validates both. `pnpm infra:deploy` and `pnpm test:e2e` run under `varlock run`, so a missing or malformed value fails before Alchemy or Playwright starts.

## Preview stages in CI
40→
`.github/workflows/preview.yml` deploys `pr-<number>` for a push to a pull request, smoke tests the stage, and destroys it when the pull request closes. It needs the repository secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, (no sign-in secret beyond `ORG_CREATION_ALLOWLIST`, which `infra/alchemy.run.ts` reads). Fork pull requests are skipped. The decision and its backtest are in ADR 0026.

The first job, `select`, decides what the revision needs before any stage work starts:

- A revision that is no longer the head of its pull request stops there, and the newer revision owns the stage. If the read of the pull request fails, the revision keeps its stage.
- `scripts/ci/select.mjs` classifies the PR's changed files, read from the compare endpoint `base...head` by commit SHA. It matches the old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename. `scripts/ci/select.test.ts` locks its rules. It sets three gates:
  - `stage` is off only when every changed file is prose or agent tooling: under `docs/`, any `*.md`, the agent instruction directories, `.githooks/`, `skills-lock.json`, or the root `scripts/`. An empty list, a mixed list or any other path deploys a stage.
  - `canary` is on when the PR touches `packages/cloudflare`, `infra`, `scripts/ci`, the answer entry (`apps/web/answer.html`, `src/answer`, `src/messages`, `vite.config.ts`), the dependency pins or this workflow.
  - `lighthouse` is on when the PR touches the answer entry, `infra/scripts/lighthouse` or `infra/package.json`.

Effect Schema is the repository's type library. Schemas should be used before hand-written guards.

scripts/ci runs as plain Node without the Effect runtime or pnpm install. select.mjs cannot import Effect Schema. Hand-written guards are required.

Discriminated unions will represent the compare decision. The public function returns gate booleans. Tests assert those gates. JSON parsing stays in main. The function receives unknown.

changedPaths returns null as an incomplete signal. A discriminated union with "paths" and "incomplete" kinds is cleaner. readCompare will return that union.

gatesFromCompare will be the exported user-facing function. readCompare can remain unexported. The isRecord helper is acceptable. GitHub may omit the previous_filename field, so jq map must handle null. Changed path extraction needs careful implementation. The type-system-discipline skill should be applied first.

The API caps changed files at 300 and does not paginate. The 3000 check was wrong. Both success and unread paths will route through select.mjs to consolidate gate decisions. The type-system-discipline and boundary-discipline leaf skills will be read fully before citation.

Tests will assert gate booleans from a compare payload rather than matching regex patterns. Boundary and type-system-discipline will be read in parallel with drafting the code.

The workflow test that reads YAML is implementation-pinned. It should assert that the workflow passes the compare payload to select.mjs and does not treat 3000 lines as the file cap. The unit test already covers the 300-file-all-gates behavior.

A regression test will verify the preview workflow no longer uses the 3000-line check and correctly invokes select.mjs. The contract between the workflow and the script is the observable wiring. Actionlint is not required locally. Proceeding to write the files.

select.mjs will be rewritten in place. The 300-file cap constant is exported. The stdin path parsing stays intact.

changedPaths now enforces the 300-file cap and returns null if the list is too long. It iterates the files array, validates each entry is a record with a string filename, and collects both filename and previous_filename when present. The function returns null if any file record is malformed. The gatesFromCompare signature is being drafted.

gatesFromCompare returns all gates when changedPaths signals incompleteness. The internal null sentinel is acceptable for laziness. The discriminated union is reserved for the public interface.

The internal helper will return a discriminated union with "paths" and "incomplete" kinds. The full type-system-discipline principle will be read before citation.

A simple if statement is sufficient for exhaustiveness checks in JavaScript. The CLI argument parser will be a plain function that returns an options object with optional compare path and unread flag.

The CLI parser now rejects missing or invalid `--compare` values and forbids combining `--unread` with `--compare`. It returns an options object with an optional compare path. Because `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` is enabled, the parser will only set `compare` when the flag is actually provided, avoiding an explicit `undefined` assignment.

The main function will write each changed path to stdout, then print the gate booleans. It appends those same values to GITHUB_OUTPUT when that environment variable is set.

The main function now handles both `--unread` and `--compare` paths. It parses arguments, returns all gates for unread mode, and for compare mode it reads the JSON file, falls back to all gates on parse failure, and returns all gates when the file list is incomplete. Valid paths are classified and written to stdout and GITHUB_OUTPUT.

The stdin fallback will split lines and strip trailing carriage returns before classifying paths. A type assertion to `unknown` is banned by lint rules, so the compare payload will be declared without an initial type annotation and parsed directly.

The runner-minutes script already uses `any` for JSON.parse results, so the new script will follow that existing pattern. `readFileSync` must be imported from `node:fs` alongside `appendFileSync`. The workflow YAML is being drafted next.

The workflow draft uses `gh api` to fetch the compare endpoint by commit SHA range. It extracts `filename` and `previous_filename` into a temporary JSON file. The script is invoked with `--compare` when the API call succeeds. Otherwise it falls back to default gates.

The workflow draft now falls back to `--unread` when the compare API call fails, printing a warning that every stage gate is required. The jq filter safely handles null `.files` and missing filenames, so Node still returns all gates. The `--paginate` flag is removed because the API only returns files on the first page, and omitting it correctly limits the output to the 300-file cap.

The ADR bullet is being updated to state that the compare endpoint returns at most 300 changed files on the first page only, with no pagination. A 300-file list keeps every gate because a shorter list cannot be distinguished from a cut-off one. The docs/infra.md line 50 is also being revised to match this behavior.

Runner-minutes now defines a 1000-run cap constant and a helper to detect when the filtered search hits it. The script throws an error if the cap is reached, advising the user to narrow the --days window. Job data is fetched by paginating the jobs endpoint for each run.

Tests will verify the jobsQuery filter and the runSearchIsCapped helper. The query builder is part of the public interface, so its observable output must be locked down. A test case with two jobs of the same name will confirm that reruns are counted in minutes.

A `requireCompleteRunSearch` helper will be exported to throw the exact capped-search error. Callers will test this exported function rather than the raw throw message. The `filter=all` fix is confirmed as the correct behavior for counting rerun minutes.

The `requireCompleteRunSearch` test will assert that 1000 runs throw an error containing "cap", while 999 runs do not. The exact error message is not required because callers do not branch on it. The GitHub workflow-run cap will be noted in the ADR.

The runner-minutes script is not listed as a gate in the ADR, so its error message and test names will carry that documentation. The test for the 1000-run cap will be named "refuses a run list that has reached GitHub's 1000-result search cap", and the rerun test will be named "asks for every attempt of a job, including reruns". # Type System Discipline

Make the compiler reject impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants.
10→

- **Derive types from authoritative schemas.** When a schema file owns a shape, derive the type from it instead of hand-rolling a parallel one.
