A comment in preview.yml mentions 3000.

The 3000 limit is in the workflow script, not preview.yml. I'll update it and grep preview.yml directly. Then I'll implement all edits and add the workflow test to select.test.ts.

I'll rewrite select.mjs by replacing the bottom portion and adding new functions after classify. I'll preserve classify and regexes exactly, keep the entry point check, and draft the full file. I'll also check line length since oxfmt will wrap.

JSDoc will remain for exported functions to satisfy checkJs. readCompareFiles does not need to be exported. gatesFromCompare is exported and tested. parseSelectArgs will be tested via CLI spawn rather than unit tests, since CLI tests better reflect workflow behavior.

I'll test gatesFromCompare directly and spawn --compare with JSON, --unread, invalid JSON, and missing files. Invalid or missing JSON files will fall back to all gates with exit 0. I also noted that any uncaught exception in select.mjs would fail the workflow job.

Only file read and JSON parse errors will be caught. A thrown classifier bug must fail the job rather than be hidden. The workflow never passes conflicting flags, so that case is not a concern.

I'll combine the file read and JSON parse into a single try block. This catches both read and parse errors, but classifier bugs remain uncaught so the job fails.

I'll test the 300-file threshold against arrays of 300 objects versus 150 objects with 300 paths. The logic must check the file count, not the total path count, to avoid wrongly keeping the stage. A non-object entry in the array will correctly return incomplete.

The gatesFromCompare unit test locks in the correct file-count logic. The workflow string test catches the old YAML bug where the script checks line count instead of file count.

The workflow test will also verify that preview.yml omits `--paginate` from the compare call. The old bug used that flag, which prevented fetching additional files and caused jq errors on empty pages. The updated workflow should pass `--compare` without pagination. The test will assert that the compare URL contains `select.mjs --compare` and `select.mjs --unread`, and that `3000` no longer appears in preview.yml.

The timeout is acceptable. I'll update the todos and write the files. The runner-minutes query uses a numeric run.id in a template string. requireCompleteRunSearch checks the run count before fetching jobs, so it never triggers 1000 job list calls on a capped window. If GitHub returns more than 1000 runs, the check is skipped and the behavior remains correct.

I'll phrase the error to reflect the 1000-run cap on filtered workflow lists. I'll also check the Link header for a next page after 1000 results.

Pagination is unnecessary because GitHub omits a next link after 1000 results, so the count itself signals truncation. I will now implement the changes, add the test, run tests, format and lint the files, and proceed to review, commit, and PR. I also verified that empty paths correctly trigger all gates.

I'll add tests for empty files, null, and non-array inputs to gatesFromCompare. I'll also verify that canary files under the cap still trigger the canary gate. I'll fix the inaccurate workflow comment while keeping the existing comment style.

Shell error handling is sound. `gh api` returns non-zero on HTTP errors, so the workflow step fails correctly. Node failures inside the `then` block also fail the step. No `set -o pipefail` is needed because there are no pipes. A file-count race condition is not a concern. The Ubuntu runner supports the jq expression. rawInput.old_string:
# The compare endpoint is addressed by commit, so the list cannot be stale after a push. It matches the
        # old `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename. It caps at 3000 files, so a list that
        # long may be cut short and keeps every gate.
        run: |
          if gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" \
              --jq '.files[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt" \
            && [ "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt")" -lt 3000 ]; then
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt"
          else
            echo "The changed files could not be read in full: every stage gate is required."
            printf 'stage=true\ncanary=true\nlighthouse=true\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
rawInput.new_string:
# The compare endpoint is addressed by commit, so the list cannot be stale after a push. It matches
        # `git diff BASE...HEAD` and includes the old name of a rename. The file list stops at 300, on the
        # first page only. select.mjs keeps every gate at that cap, and when this read fails.
        run: |
          if gh api "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" \
              --jq '{files: [.files[] | {filename, previous_filename}]}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/compare.json"; then
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs --compare "$RUNNER_TEMP/compare.json"
          else
            echo "The changed files could not be read: every stage gate is required."
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs --unread
          fi

        run: |
          if gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" \
              --jq '.files[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt" \
            && [ "$(wc -l < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt")" -lt 3000 ]; then
            node scripts/ci/select.mjs < "$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt"
          else
            echo "The changed files could not be read in full: every stage gate is required."

          fi

content.text:
Lint passed. Now running typecheck. The full run may be heavy.

Reviewing select.mjs and the workflow for correctness. The jq filter handles empty arrays. gh api without --paginate is safe because files are limited to 300. Will run the scripts and set a long block_until.

Confirmed the three-dot compare syntax matches the original `git diff BASE...HEAD` behavior. Empty diffs correctly produce an empty files array. The shell quoting for the API path is safe.

The checkout and classify steps share the same conditional guard, so a checkout failure prevents classify from running. If checkout sparse fails while classify still runs, the job fails because Node cannot find the script. Both gatesFromCompare and main implement the incomplete-to-all-gates path, but main duplicates the ALL_GATES branch instead of calling gatesFromCompare.

The duplicated logic should be consolidated. The CLI should call a single function that returns both the gate decision and the file paths. This prevents the tested function from drifting from the CLI behavior.

The CLI test only covers the catch path when the compare file cannot be read. It does not exercise the incomplete payload path through main. This leaves a small drift risk: main could diverge from gatesFromCompare on the incomplete-to-all-gates branch.

Decided to refactor main to call readCompareFiles directly and branch on its returned kind. This removes the duplicated incomplete-to-all-gates logic and aligns the CLI with the tested function.

The CLI will now call gatesFromCompare directly, removing the duplicated incomplete-to-all-gates branch from main. This unifies the decision logic between the CLI and the tested pure function. A 300-file CLI test is unnecessary because the unit test already covers the 300-file cap through gatesFromCompare.

The refactor is safe because the tested function governs the gate decision, so any drift would only affect path printing. The shell should call the pure function directly. I also need to check the runner-minutes jobsQuery formatting after oxfmt, and I can remove the `/** @type {unknown} */` annotation on `payload` by passing the JSON.parse result directly.

Type-aware lint passed, so passing the parsed payload directly to gatesFromCompare is safe. The jq filter correctly handles absent previous_filename and filename fields by producing null, which the code treats as incomplete and routes to all gates.

A single bad entry in the file list correctly triggers the all-gates fallback. The 300-file cap is safe because the logic only checks the count, not the names. Runner minutes queries using filter=all are sound: skipped jobs contribute zero minutes, and attempts remain within the same run window.

Duplicate counting is intentional: both attempts contribute minutes when both succeed. The 1000-run cap is enforced after paginating through the list endpoint, which is acceptable. The workflow_runs endpoint covers all workflows in the repository. I will run a full typecheck with a long timeout, then deslop and spawn the reviewer.

The classify step omits an explicit `shell: bash` declaration, but the default shell on Ubuntu runners is bash and `set -e` is active, so the conditional logic remains safe. A thrown error from `select.mjs` would fail the step and skip deployment, though parse failures are caught and incomplete payloads return all gates. A failed `GITHUB_OUTPUT` write would also fail the step. The `--unread` path requires the script to exist, which depends on checkout succeeding.

The checkout and classify steps share the same conditional guard, so a checkout failure correctly skips classify. The logic is sound. I will check the ADR line length for markdown lint, review the runner-minutes formatting after oxfmt, and inspect select.mjs for long lines.

The preview.yml comment about the 300-file cap is accurate and acceptable because YAML comments are not subject to the no-comments rule. Large responses from `gh api --jq` are safe.

The compare endpoint does not support file pagination, so the 300-file cap is a hard API limit. The get commit endpoint paginates up to 3000 files but only returns a single commit diff, not the three-dot PR diff, so it is unsuitable. The pulls files API is tied to pull request numbers and can become stale. Explicit per_page parameters are unnecessary.

A new `decisionFromCompare` export will return both gates and paths together. This lets `gatesFromCompare` stay a thin wrapper. Tests can then verify the gate decision without needing to call `readCompareFiles` separately.

The double read is acceptable because the file list is small. Keeping the path list in the workflow log is worth the minor duplication. The gatesFromCompare wrapper will return both gates and paths together.

Decided against merging paths into the gate object. Tests would break because `toEqual` would include extra paths. The duplication in `main` is small and acceptable. Both the CLI and the unit test use `readCompareFiles`, so the 300-file cap is enforced in both paths. The incomplete-to-all-gates branch is the only remaining drift risk, but both paths use the same check. Now running typecheck.

I will check scripts/tsconfig for a narrower typecheck if the full run is too slow. The runner-minutes formatting and jobsQuery line length need verification. I will run typecheck with a 120-second timeout and wait for the result before committing. The no-comments lint passed with zero errors, confirming JSDoc is allowed.

main duplicates the gate decision logic instead of calling gatesFromCompare.

Switching main to call gatesFromCompare would let the CLI and tests share one function. This is a small fix worth doing before review. The double file walk is acceptable. Tests of gatesFromCompare would not catch the bug if main and gatesFromCompare disagree.

gatesFromCompare handles incomplete reads by returning all gates and empty paths, so the single function stays consistent. The jobsQuery line and run.id type are fine. Now typechecking the scripts project.

The workflow test is brittle because it string-matches YAML wiring. It will be kept since the previous bug lived only in YAML. The reviewer will be spawned after the typecheck and the main refactor.

I will check the deslop skill before committing. I will not run the no-comments skill because the user rule forbids spawning other review agents on the same change.

I will self-check for slop and comments instead of spawning the deslop or comment-sicko subagents. The reviewer agent is the only one the user explicitly requested. The jq filter is fine even with a large number of files.

Missing previous_filename values are handled correctly. If the GitHub API returns a null files object, jq fails and the script falls back to --unread. The compare API always returns files as an array, so empty results are safe.

The typecheck script will be run next. The work will be committed in two separate commits: first the preview cap, then runner-minutes. I will check `but status` to see if this is a linked worktree, and omit the `-b` flag if so.

The API failure is TS6305. The domain dist is not built. This triggers cascading errors.

The fast typecheck path likely skips building dependencies first. This is a pre-existing project-reference issue in a fresh worktree. The scripts project passed. I will not chase this unrelated TS6305. CI uses the non-fast path which may emit.

I will self-review the diff and spawn the reviewer. I will leave the main function unchanged. I noted a few minor issues to fix first: double traversal is unnecessary but harmless, the workflow test is stringly typed, and the run search cap uses >= 1000 as a safe documented choice.

The `filter=all` behavior is intentional. The YAML comment is accurate. The ADR threshold matches the code. The jq expression safely handles missing `.files` by falling back to `--unread`. An empty file list correctly deploys only the stage gate.

A 300-file response triggers all-gate without checking canary status. The list may be truncated. The shell uses literal triple dots in the compare path. The script appends unread results to GITHUB_OUTPUT. This avoids overwriting prior outputs.

The classify step outputs stage correctly. If head is false, the step is skipped and deployment is blocked. SHA encoding is unnecessary. I will spawn the reviewer subagent with the brief and acceptance criteria.

I will set background false so the reviewer runs synchronously and I wait for its output before proceeding.

The reviewer kickoff prompt must include `Read <path>/worker.md` as required by the poteto-mode skill. I will verify that worker.md exists at the expected path. The reviewer will be asked to review the diff against the brief and flag any defects.

I will use the explicit `reviewer` subagent type rather than omitting it. I will prepare the commit message in parallel while the reviewer runs.

I will spawn the reviewer with background true so I can keep preparing the commit message and reading the PR playbook in parallel. I will wait for the reviewer to finish using get_command_or_subagent_output with a timeout, avoiding any polling.

The jobs query URL matches the test expectation exactly. The workflow YAML indentation needs verification. The test that checks for the 3000 file cap belongs in select.mjs, not the workflow.

The 3000 file cap was removed from preview.yml and the test passed. The official GitHub docs confirm that changed files are capped at 300 on the first page of the compare API.

I will not pass `per_page` to the compare API. That would risk truncating the file list below the documented 300-file cap. I will read the opening PR playbook and the PR skill to prepare for the shipper subagent.

1→---
name: principle-prove-it-works
description: "Apply after completing a task, before declaring done. Verify against the real artifact (run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff), not a proxy, self-report, or 'it compiles.'"
user-invocable: false
---

# Prove It Works

Verify every output by checking the real thing directly: run the feature, read the actual value, inspect the diff. Proxies (file mtimes, self-reports, cached output, "it compiles") do not count. When a check fails, suspect the observation method before the system.
10→
Before you report success (merged, sent, started), read the real state and the exit code. Truncated output (`| tail -1`) and your own echo prove nothing.

Verify the process as well as the outcome. A correct result can rest on a broken process: a clause reconstructed from the user's paste instead of the durable record, a constraint honored by chance from a file never read. For each fact you relied on, name the record it came from and confirm that record is the one the project's rules point at.

Red is a colour, not a measurement. A failing check proves the instrument only when the failure content is the disagreement you predicted. Quote the assertion's diff (`Extra items in the right set`), never the assertion (`assert {...} == {...}`). A convergence probe keys on behavior only the new artifact can produce, never an identity field the old one also emits.

Script the check when you can. A deterministic script that reruns the comparison beats a one-time look. Keep its output where the human can see it, and commit it only when the trail must be auditable later.

1→### Opening a PR

Invoked at the end of every other playbook.

Work from a git worktree off trunk, and keep unrelated work out of it. Rebase into small, landable commits. Run `/deslop` over the diff before commit. Before you commit, merge, or deploy from a worktree, list the live agents and stop every one that holds it, including grandchildren you never launched. Confirm each stop, then run `git status` and read the tree you are about to ship.

Title: `type(scope): subject`, naming a real symbol when one carries the change. Body: a one-minute briefing under 40 lines with these `##` headings in order, dropping empty ones: `## Why`, `## What changed`, `## Scope`, `## Tradeoffs` (only rejected alternatives a reviewer would otherwise ask about), `## Blast Radius`, `## Verification`.

Stack follow-ups by base branch. Open PRs ready, through the run's PR tool with `draft: false`. Without one, use `gh pr create` without `--draft`, or `origin pr create --status open` when Origin's CLI resolves the repository. Opening a PR does not start a babysit.

content.text:
I found a real bug. `gh api --jq` colorizes JSON when stdout is a TTY.

FORCE_COLOR is set in this environment, which explains the ANSI codes even when output is redirected to a file. GitHub Actions runners do not set this variable by default.

GitHub Actions runners likely do not set FORCE_COLOR. Redirected output should therefore be plain JSON in CI.

The failure is local because this agent environment sets FORCE_COLOR. To prevent ANSI codes in JSON on any runner, the workflow should explicitly disable color. `NO_COLOR` does not override `FORCE_COLOR` for `gh`, so `--color=never` or `GH_NO_COLOR=1` is needed instead.

I will pass `--color=never` to `gh api` to guarantee parseable JSON. The local reproduction confirms `JSON.parse` fails on colored output. I am now checking which environment variable is forcing color on a redirected file.

The `--color` flag must precede `api` in the `gh` command because it is global.

The `--color` flag is not recognized by this `gh` version. The output file was truncated to empty because the command failed. `CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` is set in this environment, which forces color output even when redirected. GitHub Actions does not set this variable, so CI would be unaffected. A runner image setting it would still cause the same issue.

The fix is to disable color for this call. Unsetting `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `NO_COLOR` before the `gh api` command should prevent colored output. Using `jq` directly on the raw response is another option, since `gh`'s jq printer applies color.
